title: 10.1 Hiring employees > Overview
text:
- When a business hires its first employee, it must register as an employer with **SSS**, **PhilHealth**, and **Pag-IBIG**, and follow DOLE wage rules.
- The **Central Business Portal (https://business.gov.ph)** has one employee-reporting module covering SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG.
- A self-employed owner who hires workers must also register as an employer and get an SSS Employer Number.
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employer-er/ and https://www.sss.gov.ph/self-employed/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.2 Hiring employees > SSS employer registration
text:
- SSS coverage of an employer starts on the **first day of operation**.
- Register through the Central Business Portal (no SS Form R-1 or supporting documents needed), through My.SSS online, or at an SSS branch.
- Report new employees to SSS **within 30 days from their hiring date**. Employees must have their own SS numbers.
- Each month, deduct the employee share from pay and remit it with the employer share and EC contribution, using a Payment Reference Number (PRN).
- Late contributions are charged a **2% penalty per month** until paid.
- Contribution rates are in the SSS contribution table (effective January 1, 2025): https://www.sss.gov.ph/sss-contribution-table/
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employer-er/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.3 Hiring employees > SSS for self-employed owners
text:
- A self-employed SSS member is someone who has no employer other than themself.
- Contributions are paid monthly or quarterly using a PRN from My.SSS. The deadline is the **last day of the month after** the month being paid for.
- Amounts follow the latest SSS schedule of contributions.
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/self-employed/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.4 Hiring employees > PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG
text:
- Private-sector workers with an employer–employee relationship are covered under PhilHealth's formal economy program. The member submits a PhilHealth Member Registration Form.
- Employer registration steps and premium rates for PhilHealth, and employer registration and contribution rates for Pag-IBIG, are not covered here. Ask PhilHealth or Pag-IBIG, or register through the Central Business Portal (https://business.gov.ph).
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/members/formal/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.8 Hiring employees > When to remit Pag-IBIG contributions (deadlines)
text:
- Pag-IBIG asks all registered employers to use the **Electronic Submission of Remittance Schedule (eSRS)** through **Virtual Pag-IBIG for Employers** to pay employees' membership savings and loan payments. After submitting the remittance schedule online, you get a **Payment Reference Number** to pay through accredited collecting partners.
- **Due dates** depend on the first letter of the employer's name:
 
- A to F: 1st to 7th day of the month after the period covered
 
- G to N: 5th to 11th day of the month after
 
- O to Z, numbers or special characters: 9th to 15th day of the month after
- Applies to employers in Baguio City and Benguet.
Source: https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/ESRS.html (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.5 Hiring employees > Minimum wage in Baguio City and Benguet (Cordillera, CAR)
text:
- Baguio City and all Benguet towns (including La Trinidad, Tuba, and Itogon) are in the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), so the CAR wage orders apply.
- Private sector: **₱505.00 per day** under **Wage Order No. CAR-24**, effective **December 30, 2025**.
- Domestic workers (kasambahay): **₱6,600.00 per month** under **Wage Order No. CAR-DW-07**, effective December 30, 2025.
- Wage orders change. Check the National Wages and Productivity Commission for the current order: https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/
Source: https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.10 Hiring employees > Pag-IBIG for a kasambahay (household employee)
text:
- Under the Batas Kasambahay (RA 10361), Pag-IBIG membership is **mandatory** once a kasambahay has worked for **at least one month**. The household employer must ensure registration and regular, correct remittance.
- Covered: general househelp, yaya, cook, gardener, laundry person, and others regularly doing household work for one household (including live-out). Family drivers, service providers and occasional helpers may join as voluntary members.
- The kasambahay registers online at Virtual Pag-IBIG (membership category: Employed – Private Household), gets the MID number after 2–3 working days, and gives it to the employer. Applies in Baguio City and Benguet.
Source: https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/HouseholdEmployeeMembership.html (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.10 Hiring employees > Who pays the kasambahay's Pag-IBIG contribution
text:
Pag-IBIG's sharing rule for household employees (kasambahay):
- Monthly salary **₱1,500 or less**: the employer pays everything (3% of monthly salary).
- **More than ₱1,500 up to ₱4,999**: the employer pays everything (4% of monthly salary).
- **₱5,000 or more**: the kasambahay pays 2% and the employer pays 2%, up to a maximum fund salary of ₱10,000 (e.g., ₱5,000 salary: ₱100 + ₱100).
- The employer's share **cannot be deducted** from the kasambahay's salary. Extra savings above the required amount are voluntary and the employer does not have to match them.
Source: https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/HouseholdEmployeeMembership.html (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.9 Hiring employees > Where to find DOLE rules on 13th month pay and holiday pay
text:
- DOLE's Bureau of Working Conditions (BWC) publishes the official guidance on pay rules. In 2026 it issued **Labor Advisory No. 21-26, Guidelines on the Payment of Thirteenth Month Pay**, and **Labor Advisory No. 17-26** on wages for regular holidays and special days in **2027**. These apply in Baguio City and Benguet too.
- BWC also publishes the **Workers' Statutory Monetary Benefits Handbook (2024 edition)** and FAQs on 13th month pay.
- This knowledge base does not contain the computation rules. Read them at the BWC site or ask the DOLE Baguio–Benguet Field Office (see 17.8).
Source: https://bwc.dole.gov.ph/issuances/labor-advisories/ and https://bwc.dole.gov.ph/workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.6 Hiring employees > Registering the business with DOLE (Rule 1020)
text:
- **Every establishment, whatever its size**, must register with DOLE under **Rule 1020 of the Occupational Safety and Health Standards**, so it is part of DOLE's list of covered establishments. This applies to private businesses operating in the Philippines.
- The form is the Registry of Establishment. Legal basis: DOLE Department Order No. 198-18 (rules of the OSH law, RA 11058).
- In Baguio City and Benguet, register with the **DOLE Baguio–Benguet Field Office**, DOLE-CAR New Building, Cabinet Hill, Baguio City; (074) 442-2447; car_baguiobenguet@dole.gov.ph.
Source: https://ro7.dole.gov.ph/frontline-services/ and https://car.dole.gov.ph/contact-us/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 10.6 Hiring employees > How to register your business with DOLE online (Online Compliance Portal)
text:
- DOLE's **Online Compliance Portal (OCP)** at https://reports.dole.gov.ph is where an establishment **registers with DOLE** (see 10.6 for the Rule 1020 duty) and can **verify its DOLE registration certificate**. Click **Sign Up** to create an account, then log in to register the establishment and manage submissions.
- The same portal is used to submit the Work Accident/Illness Report, the **13th Month Pay Report**, Telecommuting and Flexible Work Arrangements reports, and labor inspection forms.
- Technical help: ocptechsupport@bwc.dole.gov.ph. Businesses in Baguio City and Benguet can also ask the DOLE Baguio–Benguet Field Office (see 17.8).

title: 10.6 Hiring employees > What safety documents DOLE-CAR asks for during inspection
text:
DOLE-CAR (Cordillera, which covers Baguio City and Benguet) lists these as **requirements for inspection** on its downloadable forms page:
- An **OSH (occupational safety and health) Program**. DOLE-CAR provides a template for **micro establishments** and a separate one for small, medium and large establishments.
- Workplace policies and programs on a drug-free workplace, Hepatitis B, HIV and AIDS prevention, and tuberculosis prevention.
- Health reports: Report on Health and Safety Organization, Employer's Work Accident/Illness Report, Annual Work Accident/Illness Exposure Data Report, and Annual Medical Report.
The templates can be downloaded and edited.
Source: https://car.dole.gov.ph/downloadable-links/ (checked November 23, 2026)

title: 11.1 Customer discounts > PWD discount: what businesses must give
text:
- Persons with disabilities get **at least 20% discount and VAT exemption** (if applicable) on goods and services for their exclusive use, including: hotels, restaurants, and recreation centers; admission to theaters, cinemas, and similar venues; medicines in drugstores; medical and dental services; domestic air and sea fares; land transport fares; and funeral and burial services. (RA 10754)
- Proof: a PWD ID issued by the city or municipal mayor or barangay captain, the PWD's passport, or a transportation discount ID from the national council.
- The PWD discount cannot be combined with a higher discount or another discount program.
Source: https://ncda.gov.ph/disability-laws/republic-acts/republic-act-no-10754-an-act-expanding-the-benefits-and-privileges-of-persons-with-disability-pwd/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 11.1 Customer discounts > PWD discount: tax deduction for the business
text:
- A business can claim the PWD discount it gave (except on government medical services) as a **tax deduction**, based on the net cost of the goods sold or services rendered, in the same taxable year, with proper documentation. (RA 10754)
- For the senior citizen discount, see 11.2.
Source: https://ncda.gov.ph/disability-laws/republic-acts/republic-act-no-10754-an-act-expanding-the-benefits-and-privileges-of-persons-with-disability-pwd/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 11.2 Customer discounts > Senior citizen discount: what businesses must give
text:
- Senior citizens (resident Filipino citizens aged **60 or older**) get a **20% discount and VAT exemption** (if applicable) on goods and services for their exclusive use, including: medicines and some vaccines; doctors' fees and medical, dental, and lab services in private facilities; land transport, domestic air and sea fares; **hotels and lodging, restaurants, and recreation centers**; admission to theaters, cinemas, and amusement places; and funeral and burial services. (RA 9994)
- Applies to businesses in Baguio City and Benguet like everywhere in the Philippines.
Source: https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/post/what-are-the-rights-and-privileges-of-senior-citizens (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 11.2 Customer discounts > Senior citizen discount: proof, promos, and combining discounts
text:
- Proof the senior can show: an **OSCA ID** (from the Office of Senior Citizens Affairs; honored nationwide), a passport, or other documents proving citizenship and age 60+.
- If an item is already on promo, the senior gets either the promo discount or the 20% discount, **whichever is higher**, not both.
- The National Commission of Senior Citizens says discounts follow the rules on promotional discounts and the prohibition on combining discounts, after an October 2026 Supreme Court ruling.
- NCSC contact: (02) 8567-5646, contact@ncsc.gov.ph.
Source: https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/post/what-are-the-rights-and-privileges-of-senior-citizens and https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/post/pahayag-ng-ncsc-sa-no-double-discount-ruling-ng-korte-suprema (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 11.2 Customer discounts > Senior citizen discount: tax deduction for the business
text:
- A business can claim the senior citizen discounts it gave as a **tax deduction**, based on the cost of the goods sold or services rendered, in the same taxable year. The amount, net of VAT, must be included in gross sales receipts and properly documented under the Tax Code. (RA 9994)
Source: https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/post/what-are-the-rights-and-privileges-of-senior-citizens (checked November 23, 2026)

title: 12.1 Tourism businesses > DOT accreditation: mandatory or optional
text:
- Under the Tourism Act of 2009 (RA 9593) and its implementing rules, accreditation by the Department of Tourism (DOT) is **compulsory for primary tourism enterprises** and **voluntary for secondary tourism enterprises**. This applies in Baguio City and Benguet like everywhere in the Philippines.
- **Prior DOT accreditation is required before the LGU issues a license or permit to operate a primary tourism enterprise.** So a homestay, inn or tour operator in Baguio City needs DOT accreditation before it gets the city business permit, the Mayor's Permit (see 02).
- The DOT can fine, downgrade, suspend or revoke accreditation after notice and hearing, and tells the LGU when an enterprise fails to get or loses accreditation.
Source: https://mirror.officialgazette.gov.ph/2009/11/10/implementing-rules-and-regulations-of-republic-act-no-9593/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 12.2 Tourism businesses > Which businesses are primary (DOT accreditation required)
text:
Primary tourism enterprises (DOT accreditation mandatory), as listed in the RA 9593 rules:
- **Travel and tour services:** inbound travel agencies and tour operators, local tour operators, ecotour operators and **tour guides**.
- **Accommodation:** hotels, resorts, apartment hotels, **tourist inns**, motels, **pension houses**, **private homes used for homestay**, ecolodges, condotels, serviced apartments, and **bed and breakfast** facilities.
- **Tourist transport** (land, sea, air) whose seats are only or mostly for tourists, including airport taxis and tourist drivers.
- Also: event and convention organizers, dive shops, amusement parks, and adventure and ecotourism facilities.
A homestay, tourist inn, pension house or tour guide in Baguio City or Benguet therefore falls under mandatory accreditation.
Source: https://mirror.officialgazette.gov.ph/2009/11/10/implementing-rules-and-regulations-of-republic-act-no-9593/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 12.3 Tourism businesses > Which businesses are secondary (DOT accreditation optional)
text:
Secondary tourism enterprises (DOT accreditation voluntary), as listed in the RA 9593 rules: restaurants; specialty shops and department stores; museums, galleries, theme parks and zoos; spas and other health and wellness facilities; rest areas in gas stations; **agri-tourism farms**; tourism training centers and trainers; and outbound travel agencies.
- For example, a restaurant, souvenir or pasalubong shop, or strawberry or vegetable farm open to tourists in Baguio City or Benguet may apply for DOT accreditation but is not required to.
- Only accredited enterprises benefit from DOT promotion, training and other programs.
Source: https://mirror.officialgazette.gov.ph/2009/11/10/implementing-rules-and-regulations-of-republic-act-no-9593/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 12.4 Tourism businesses > How to apply for DOT accreditation
text:
- DOT accreditation is applied for online through the DOT Accreditation Portal: https://accreditation.tourism.gov.ph (create an account, then sign in).
- The portal's public page shows only the sign-in screen. The current list of documents, inspection steps and any accreditation fee are **not published on a page we could read**, so this knowledge base does not have them. The chatbot should give no fee or document list and refer the user to the DOT or the portal.
- In Baguio City, accommodation establishments must also register in the city's VISITA system (see 12.5).
Source: https://accreditation.tourism.gov.ph/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: FOR VALIDATION)

title: 12.5 Tourism businesses > Baguio City VISITA registration for accommodations
text:
- Under Baguio City's **VISITA Ordinance (Ordinance No. 20, s. 2026)**, accommodation establishments register in the city's VISITA system at https://visita.baguio.gov.ph. Its listing includes hotels, homestays, transient houses, boarding houses and condo units for rent.
- Registration collects the establishment's registered name, business address, contact details and supporting permits, for **accreditation, monitoring and regulation** of tourism establishments. Data is shared with the Business Permits and Licensing Office and the DOT for validation.
- The VISITA site publishes each establishment's name, type, general location, and licensing and accreditation status.
- Office: **City Tourism, Culture and Arts Office**, Baguio Convention and Cultural Center; (074) 446 2009; baguiovisita@gmail.com.
Source: https://visita.baguio.gov.ph/auth/register and https://visita.baguio.gov.ph/contact (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 13.1 Food businesses > Sanitary permit
text:
- Under the Code on Sanitation (PD 856, Section 14), **no one may operate a food establishment open to the public without a sanitary permit from the local health office.** A food establishment is any place where food or drinks are made, processed, stored, sold or served, which includes carinderias, food stalls, eateries and bakeries.
- The sanitary permit must be **posted in a conspicuous place**.
- Fees are set by the city or municipality. Within 14 days after a change of owner or occupant, the new occupant must have the change noted on the permit.
- In Baguio City, the health or sanitary clearance from the **City Health Services Office (CHSO)** is one of the Mayor's Permit requirements (see 02.3). The CHSO's current fee and document list are not in this knowledge base; ask the CHSO.
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1975/12/23/presidential-decree-no-856-s-1975/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 13.2 Food businesses > Health certificates for food handlers
text:
- Under PD 856 (Sections 15 and 19), **no person may be employed in a food establishment without a health certificate** from the local health authority. It is issued only after the required physical and medical examinations and immunizations.
- Food handlers must wear clean working clothes (cooks wear caps; hairnets or caps for female staff), keep good personal hygiene, and wash hands with soap and water before work and after using the toilet.
- In Baguio City, health certificates are issued by the City Health Services Office. The specific tests, validity period and fee are **not on an official page we could read**; the chatbot should not state them and should refer the user to the CHSO.
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1975/12/23/presidential-decree-no-856-s-1975/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 13.3 Food businesses > Carinderias, food stalls and home-based food in Baguio City
text:
- A carinderia or food stall in Baguio City needs the usual registrations (DTI business name, barangay clearance, Mayor's Permit, BIR) plus the **sanitary permit** (see 13.1) and **health certificates** for everyone who handles food (see 13.2). A step-by-step checklist is in section 18 (see 18.2).
- PD 856 requires food to come from sources approved by the local health authority.
- **Home-based food businesses:** PD 856 defines a food establishment by what is done there, not by size or location. Whether a home kitchen selling food needs a sanitary permit is decided by the City Health Services Office; ask them. A home-based business still needs a business permit (see 01.5).
- Packaged or processed food products may also need FDA registration (see 01.7).
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1975/12/23/presidential-decree-no-856-s-1975/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, FOR VALIDATION)

title: 13.5 Food businesses > Sanitary permit and health certificate in Tuba, Benguet
text:
In Tuba, Benguet, every business needs a sanitary permit before its business permit is issued or renewed, and food handlers need health certificates after laboratory exams and a food safety orientation. Labs at the Municipal Health Services Office (as of Jan 1, 2025): fecalysis ₱60, urinalysis ₱60, HBsAg ₱135. Fees, paid at the Treasury Office: sanitary permit ₱115 per business, health certificate ₱170 per food handler (₱285 for one business with one handler); about 1 hour. Water refilling or delivery businesses also need water analysis and a certificate of potability.
Source: https://www.tuba.gov.ph/offices/municipal-health-office/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 13.6 Food businesses > Sanitary permit and health certificate in La Trinidad, Benguet
text:
In La Trinidad, Benguet, the Municipal Health Services Office (MHSO) Sanitation Division issues the sanitary permit (PD 856) for food and non-food establishments. Bring the application form, laboratory results from any licensed laboratory, food handler's certificate (MHSO class every Tuesday, 3 PM; valid 3 years), health certificates, and a water potability certificate as appropriate. Health certificates: food establishment workers need chest X-ray, CBC, urinalysis and fecalysis; other establishments chest X-ray, CBC and urinalysis; videoke bars and night spots add VDRL/RPR. The La Trinidad MHSO fee for each health certificate is ₱50. MHSO: (074) 620-5907.
Source: https://www.latrinidadbenguet.com/municipal-health-services-office (checked November 24, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 13.4 Food businesses > Sanitary permit and health certificate in Itogon, Benguet
text:
In Itogon, Benguet, the Municipal Health Services Office issues sanitary permits and health certificates. Bring a barangay clearance, the application form and Mayor's permit form (Mayor's Office) and laboratory results. Steps: present documents at the health office for an order of payment, pay at the Treasury Office, then go to Environmental Health Services for the laboratory exam, consultation and issuance of the sanitary permit. Fees follow the municipal revenue code (amount not listed). Eateries, bakeries, street food vendors and caterers also need health certificates (X-ray, stool exam) and a food handler's certificate.
Source: https://itogon.gov.ph/2024/07/citizens-charter/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 14.1 Online selling > Do online sellers need to register?
text:
- **DTI:** if you do business under a name other than your own true name (for example a shop name on Facebook, Shopee, Lazada or TikTok Shop), you must register that business name with DTI (see 01.2). A business name registration does not let you operate; you still need a Business/Mayor's Permit.
- **BIR:** online sellers, vloggers, bloggers, online streamers, social media influencers, YouTubers and content creators register with BIR as **self-employed individuals** using BIR Form 1901 (BIR checklist CDR F1101, revised July 2025). Register on or before starting the business.
- **Baguio City:** online sellers also need a city business permit and must follow the Internet Transactions Act (see 07.5 and 02).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq and https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/CDR%20-%202025%20(1).pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 14.2 Online selling > How online sellers register with BIR
text:
BIR's Taxpayer's Guide for Online Sellers lists these channels:
- **In person:** New Business Registration Counter of the Revenue District Office (RDO) covering the place of business, or covering your residence if you sell from home. In Baguio City this is RDO No. 8; La Trinidad has RDO No. 9 (see 17.6).
- **Online:** ORUS (https://orus.bir.gov.ph/home), the NewBizReg portal, or the Philippine Business Hub (https://business.gov.ph).
- **Documents (individual):** BIR Form 1901, a government-issued ID showing name, address and birthdate, the DTI certificate if you use a business name, and either BIR Printed Invoices or a sample of your own invoices.
- **Fee:** ₱30 documentary stamp tax. You receive the Certificate of Registration (COR) and the Notice to Issue Invoice.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/TAXPAYERS%20GUIDE%20FOR%20ONLINE%20SELLERS.pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 14.3 Online selling > Duties after BIR registration
text:
From BIR's Taxpayer's Guide for Online Sellers:
- Display the BIR Certificate of Registration and Notice to Issue Invoice in the business establishment. Online sellers must also show their BIR registration on their online store (see 07.5).
- Register books of accounts before the deadline of the first quarterly or annual income tax return, whichever is earlier, and keep books and records for 5 years.
- Issue a registered invoice for every sale of ₱500 or more; if single sales are below ₱500 but the day's total is ₱500 or more, issue one invoice for the day's total. VAT-registered sellers issue an invoice for every sale.
- Sellers with yearly sales over ₱3,000,000 must have their books audited by an independent CPA.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/TAXPAYERS%20GUIDE%20FOR%20ONLINE%20SELLERS.pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 14.4 Online selling > Selling on Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop and other e-marketplaces
text:
- BIR Revenue Regulations No. 16-2023: **all online sellers must register with BIR on or before starting business on an e-marketplace platform.** E-marketplace operators must require sellers to submit their BIR Certificate of Registration (BIR Form 2303) as part of seller accreditation.
- Payments to a seller through a platform or e-wallet must go to the seller's **BIR-registered trade name**, not a personal account.
- The BIR rules define e-marketplaces (online shopping marketplaces, food delivery platforms, and booking platforms for hotels, inns, homes and rooms) but do not name specific companies. Each platform's own seller sign-up steps are not covered by official sources; check the platform's seller center.
- This applies to online sellers in Baguio City and Benguet like everywhere else.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%2016-2023.pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 14.5 Online selling > Withholding tax on platform payouts
text:
- Under RR 16-2023, e-marketplace operators withhold **1% on one-half of the gross remittances** they pay to sellers (in effect 0.5% of gross remittances). BIR announced platforms would start withholding on **July 15, 2024**.
- It does not apply if the seller's gross remittances for the past year, or so far in the current year, have not exceeded **₱500,000**, or if the seller is exempt or taxed at a lower rate and gives the platform proof.
- Gross remittance excludes returns and discounts, separately billed shipping, VAT, and the platform's own fees.
- BIR says withholding is not a new tax: the amount withheld is credited against the seller's income tax.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%2016-2023.pdf and https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/PR41JUL1624.pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 15.1 Closing a business > Overview: what to close in Baguio City
text:
Closing a sole proprietorship in Baguio City or Benguet involves separate offices:
1. **Retire the Mayor's Permit** with the city or municipality (Baguio City: City Hall) (see 15.2).
2. **Close the BIR registration** with BIR Form 1905 (see 15.3 and 01.6).
3. **Cancel the DTI business name** if the business stops before the registration expires (see 15.4 and 01.2).
4. If the business had employees, ask SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG about closing the employer account; this knowledge base does not have their closure steps (see 17).
A business that stops without closing its BIR registration stays liable for returns, taxes and penalties (see 01.6).
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1991/10/10/republic-act-no-7160/ and https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/CDR%20-%202025%20(1).pdf and https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, FOR VALIDATION)

title: 15.5 Closing a business > If you have employees: DOLE notice and separation pay
text:
DTI's closing-a-business guide lists these labor rules when a business with employees closes, including in Baguio City and Benguet: - Give **written notice to the employees and to DOLE at least one month before** the closure date. - The closure must be genuine (bona fide). - Pay **termination pay of at least half a month's pay per year of service, or one month's pay, whichever is higher** (Labor Code). SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG closure steps are not in this knowledge base (see 15.1).
Source: https://www.dti.gov.ph/dti-business-center/dti-closing-a-business/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 15.2 Closing a business > Retiring the business permit in Baguio City
text:
- Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160, Section 145), a business that stops must **submit a sworn statement of its gross sales or receipts for the current year**. If the tax already paid that year is less than the tax due on those sales, **the difference must be paid before the business is considered officially retired**.
- In Baguio City, business retirement (closure) is handled at City Hall (see 02.6). The eBPLS portal (https://ebpls.baguio.gov.ph) lists new permits, renewals and tax payments online, but not business retirement.
- The Baguio City document list and fees for retirement are not on an official page we could read. Ask the Permits and Licensing Division or the City Treasurer's Office (see 09.1). In Benguet towns, ask the municipal BPLO.
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1991/10/10/republic-act-no-7160/ and https://ebpls.baguio.gov.ph/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, FOR VALIDATION)

title: 15.2 Closing a business > Retiring the business permit in La Trinidad, Benguet
text:
In La Trinidad, Benguet, a business that stops must apply for retirement (surrender) at the Business Permits Licensing Section within 20 days, and it cannot be retired until all past and current taxes are paid (BPLS Citizen's Charter). Bring: the retirement form; barangay certification that the business is closed; the current year's original permit and plate (or affidavit of loss); Municipal Treasury Office clearance; a board resolution for corporations. The Treasury Office also asks for a sworn statement of gross sales or last year's ITR. The La Trinidad BPLS certification fee for a business record is ₱50.
Source: https://www.latrinidadbenguet.com/business-permits-and-licensing-section (checked November 24, 2026)
(Status: FOR VALIDATION)

title: 15.3 Closing a business > Closing BIR registration (Form 1905)
text:
BIR checklist (revised July 2025) for closure of business, head office or branch:
- BIR Form 1905 (2 originals).
- List of ending inventory of goods and supplies, including capital goods.
- Inventory of unused invoices, together with the unused invoices and other unused accounting forms (vouchers, delivery receipts, purchase orders).
- Original BIR notices and permits (such as the Authority to Print) and the original Certificate of Registration.
- Fee: ₱30 documentary stamp tax on the Tax Clearance Certificate issued for the closure.
- If a representative files: a Special Power of Attorney plus IDs of the owner and the representative.
In Baguio City and Benguet, file at your BIR Revenue District Office (see 17.6).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/CDR%20-%202025%20(1).pdf (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 15.4 Closing a business > Cancelling the DTI business name
text:
- Grounds for cancelling a DTI business name include stopping the business before the registration expires, or selling it (see 01.2).
- BNRS says cancellation is done at selected DTI offices: **call your DTI Regional or Provincial Office first** to ask which DTI office or Negosyo Center near you offers it. For Baguio City and Benguet, that is the DTI Benguet Provincial Office (see 17.1).
- DTI may also cancel a business name on its own, for example after it receives notice that the owner's business permit or license was cancelled.
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 15.4 Closing a business > Documents to cancel a DTI business name (sole proprietor)
text:
Closing a sole proprietorship in Baguio City or Benguet? DTI says you **must apply to cancel the business name**. Requirements: 1. Other BN-Related Application Form (Annex D) signed by the owner; 2. one valid ID of the owner; 3. a **sworn declaration** that the cancellation does not defraud creditors and that you have no outstanding business debts, or have notified all creditors; 4. if filed by a representative, an authorization letter and their ID; 5. the cancellation fee (amount not on the page; ask DTI Benguet, see 17.1). Corporations and partnerships follow a different list.
Source: https://www.dti.gov.ph/dti-business-center/dti-closing-a-business/ (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED)

title: 16.1 Transport livelihoods > Tricycle franchise in Baguio City and Benguet
text:
- Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160, Sections 447 and 458), the **city or municipal council (Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan) regulates tricycles and grants tricycle franchises** within its territory, following Department of Transportation guidelines.
- So a tricycle franchise in Baguio City is granted by the city, and in a Benguet town such as La Trinidad by that municipality.
- BIR registration of a common carrier requires a copy of its franchise documents (for example a Certificate of Public Convenience).

title: 18.1 Business-type checklists > Sari-sari store in Baguio City
text:
Steps for a sari-sari store in Baguio City (a guide, not an official list):
1. Register the store name with DTI (see 01.2).
2. Get the barangay business clearance (see 02.3).
3. Apply for the Mayor's Permit through eBPLS or the Permits and Licensing Division (see 02.2–02.4).
4. Register with BIR on or before the first sale (see 01.6).
5. If you hire helpers, register as an employer with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG (see 10).
6. Follow DTI selling rules: price tags, labels, no candy as change (see 07.4).
If you will sell cooked food, follow the food stall checklist too (see 18.2). For fees in Baguio City, ask the City Treasurer's Office (see 08.3).
Source: sections 01.2, 01.6, 02, 07.4, 08.3 and 10 of this knowledge base (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, INTERVIEW-DERIVED)

title: 18.2 Business-type checklists > Food stall or carinderia in Baguio City
text:
Steps for a food stall, carinderia or eatery in Baguio City (a guide, not an official list):
1. Register the business name with DTI (see 01.2).
2. Get the barangay business clearance (see 02.3).
3. Get health certificates for everyone who will handle food (see 13.2) and the sanitary permit/clearance from the City Health Services Office (see 13.1).
4. Apply for the Mayor's Permit (see 02.2–02.4); other clearances such as fire safety are also needed (see 02.3).
5. Register with BIR on or before the first sale (see 01.6).
6. If you hire workers, register with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG and pay at least the CAR minimum wage (see 10).
Selling packaged food products? You may also need FDA registration (see 01.7).
Source: sections 01.2, 01.6, 02.3, 10 and 13 of this knowledge base (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, INTERVIEW-DERIVED)

title: 18.3 Business-type checklists > Homestay or small inn in Baguio City
text:
Steps for a homestay, pension house or small inn in Baguio City (a guide, not an official list):
1. Register the business name with DTI (see 01.2).
2. Apply for **DOT accreditation** through the DOT Accreditation Portal; homestays and inns are primary tourism enterprises, and the city needs DOT accreditation before it issues the permit (see 12.1–12.4).
3. Register in Baguio City's **VISITA** system with the City Tourism, Culture and Arts Office (see 12.5).
4. Get the barangay clearance and the Mayor's Permit (see 02.3–02.4).
5. Register with BIR (see 01.6). If guests book through online booking platforms, BIR platform rules apply (see 14.4).
6. If you hire staff, register with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG (see 10).
Source: sections 01.2, 01.6, 02, 10, 12 and 14 of this knowledge base (checked November 23, 2026)
(Status: VERIFIED, FOR VALIDATION)

title: 18.4 Business-type checklists > Online shop in Baguio City
text:
Steps for an online shop run from Baguio City (Facebook, Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop or your own website), a guide, not an official list:
1. Register your shop name with DTI if it is not your own name (see 14.1, 01.2).
2. Get the barangay clearance and the Baguio City Mayor's Permit; a home-based online business still needs a permit (see 01.5, 02).
3. Register with BIR as a self-employed online seller on or before you start selling (see 14.1–14.2).
4. Give your BIR Certificate of Registration to the platform; platforms may withhold tax on payouts (see 14.4–14.5).
5. Follow the Internet Transactions Act and show your BIR registration online (see 07.5).
6. If you hire workers, register with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG (see 10).
Source: sections 01.2, 01.5, 02, 07.5, 10 and 14 of this knowledge base (checked November 23, 2026)

title: 18.5 Business-type checklists > Home-based service business in Baguio City
text:
Steps for a home-based service (for example tutoring, repairs, sewing, baking to order, haircuts or manicure) in Baguio City, a guide, not an official list:
1. Register a business name with DTI if you will not use your own name (see 01.2).
2. Get the barangay clearance and the Mayor's Permit; you need an identifiable place of business but not a separate office (see 01.5, 02).
3. Register with BIR as self-employed using BIR Form 1901 (see 01.6, 14.2).
4. **Barbers, beauty parlors, hairdressing and manicure services** need a sanitary permit, and workers serving customers need health certificates (PD 856, Chapter XII). Selling food made at home has its own rules (see 13.3).
5. If you hire helpers, register with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG (see 10).
Source: https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1975/12/23/presidential-decree-no-856-s-1975/ and sections 01.2, 01.5, 01.6, 02, 10, 13 and 14 of this knowledge base (checked November 23, 2026)
